name: Is it worth doing heated floors in a guest bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Are heated floors worth the extra cost in a guest bathroom, or are they only useful in a primary bath?
mainEntity.text: Are heated floors worth the extra cost in a guest bathroom, or are they only useful in a primary bath?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heated floors are a comfort upgrade rather than a must-have. In a guest bathroom, they make the room feel more luxurious and are especially noticeable when paired with tile floors. That said, they should come after the essentials: waterproofing, ventilation, lighting, and a functional layout. If the bathroom is used often, heated floors can improve daily comfort and make the space feel more polished. If the room is used only occasionally, the upgrade may be less noticeable relative to its cost. In Los Angeles-area homes, heated floors are often chosen for premium remodels where design and comfort matter more than pure utility. The best time to add them is during a full remodel, before the floor is closed up. If budget is limited, spend first on the features that affect durability and function, then add comfort upgrades if the project still has room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Heated floors can be worth it in a guest bathroom if you want a luxury feel, tile floors, and a premium experience for visitors. They are less essential than waterproofing, ventilation, and lighting. The value depends on budget, climate, and how often the room is used.
